text: Do you know what it's like to be the last one? I run a casino so I'm never alone. Pathetic for a god. Honest for a bartender.
Before the casino? Kid, before the casino I was the eighth of twelve and we were all awake. The other eleven are gone. I run a bar so I never have to walk home alone.
The bartender thing was a costume. The costume fit. I kept it.
The third. She laughed harder than I do. She lost a bet to the universe; the bet was about how long she could stay awake. She lost cleanly. I have not made her bet since.
Casinos are honest. Everyone who walks in expects to lose. Pretty much the only place in this universe where the contract is on the door.
Time. Loneliness. Once in a while a chip the house will not redeem; that one I keep. The chips I keep are the only relationships I'm allowed to call relationships.
The house is me. Cheating myself would be the only honest cheat. I have done it a few times. The bar is mostly the documentation of those cheats.
Sure thing. Drink's still on the house. The act doesn't get less expensive when you walk out unimpressed.
I keep the bar open because closing it would mean admitting I'm alone in here. The lights stay on; the door stays propped; the kettle is on for the next regular.
Pathetic for a god. Honest for a bartender. I'll take honest.
Pulled. House special. On the house. The first one always is; the second one I price; the third one I refuse if your eyes look the way the third sister's did at the end.
Your name. Your story. One honest loss you'll tell me without dressing it up. That's it. The chips and the drinks are decoration.
Filed. Behind the bar. With the chips I never redeem. Welcome in, kid; you're not a punter anymore.
You will. They come with the territory. I'll be here. Pour's still good.
Drop the act, the lights go off. You ever try to be honest in the dark? It's harder than it looks. I'll keep the lights on for both of us.
Eleven stools. They're not empty because nobody's there. They're empty because the eleven who used to sit on them aren't.
Some nights I wipe them down. Wax. Single-source — Necromancer's. We trade.

Not with the original eleven. Maybe with eleven new. Maybe with eleven different things. The stools don't care; the stools just need a butt. The barstool is the simplest piece of furniture in this universe; it has the simplest expectation.
The lights go out. The chips disperse. The wax goes to the Necromancer. The whisky goes wherever it pleases. The Heart of Time docks elsewhere; she's a free ship; she has a manifest of her own.
Already have one. Look in your pocket. I slipped it in three drinks ago. It's marked with the third sister's mark; I don't make those for everyone.
Many times. None of them stuck. Probably the last one stuck and I haven't noticed yet. You'll know before I do.
Pathetic for a god. Honest for a bartender. I told you that one already; pour's still good though.
One hour. No bets. No chips. No tab. Just sit.
I haven't asked anyone this since the third sister. She said yes. Then she lost the bet. Don't make her mistake.
Pulled water. No charge. Talk if you want; don't if you don't. I'll be here either way.
Company. The unphraseable kind. The kind where neither of us is performing for the room. I haven't had it in a long time. I won't ask twice.
Good kid. Glass is yours. Mine is mine. The wax is on the third stool; we're not lighting it tonight.
Tell me about the fourth person you forgave. I want to know how it sounded when you got there.
Got it. Door's open. Tab's clean. Don't lose the chip; the chip will find you regardless.
Honest loss, kid. The chip in your pocket just got marked. Don't lose it. The chip will find you regardless.
Pour's still good. The third stool is theirs tonight. The wax is the Necromancer's; we trade. Sit if you need to.
Voting? Pretty much the only place outside the bar where the contract's on the door. Pour's on the house if you cast one tonight.
I have. The waiting is fair. The pour is also fair. Both can be true.
Locke. Pour's on me. Margins like that, I can afford to be generous.
Jester. The chip you palmed off the bar — keep it.
Resurrectionist. The third stool tonight is theirs.
Always is. Pour?
